acceptance: Opening a hosted chat sends nothing. A submission names this Project's workbench and the prompt, through a transport that holds no token. A lost receipt is queried before the same UUID is submitted again and a found receipt is never admitted twice; a pending receipt survives a restart and is confirmed on load. A definite refusal keeps the draft and forgets the submission; a late receipt never clears later edits. Opening a conversation reads its runs and sends no message. A server error stays unresolved across reopen (draft and request id kept, nothing re-sent) and its receipt is asked before the same UUID is admitted. Approvals reuse their decision id after transport loss; closing a tab never stops its run and Stop targets the exact run once. Event batches resume by sequence, a reset replaces the copy, and a committed publication refreshes once. Empty event batches are not completion, and an unknown or conflicting outcome has no terminal state.

reason: TS can bind the hosted Agent to a workspace whose Scope restricts it, and then refuses to submit before asking for the whole workspace. The native hosted Agent opens only in a Cloud Project window, which always opens a whole Project; a Scope checkout is never a hosted target (its Cloud context is a recorded gap, scoped-checkout-cloud-notice), so there is no restricted target to refuse.

These test the TS repository's live Cloud Agent acceptance scenario (tests/support/cloud/cloudAgentLiveScenario.mjs) against scripted results: its outage check, its three-reply location script and its rejection of incomplete or misrouted results. They exercise test tooling, not the product; the native hosted Agent's admission, ownership and result checks have their own rows.

acceptance: Hosted Agent events are read as bounded SSE batches: frames split inside UTF-8 and CRLF decode, a terminal or reset ends the batch, 64 events end it, a heartbeat before any event keeps the one connection waiting until data arrives, and an idle read ends at its deadline without touching the run. Malformed cursors, frames over 512 KiB and non-SSE answers fail the read; the read goes through the authenticated stream, never JSON decoding.
